pages.text: Late anomalies learn to hide, as tumours do: they shed the markers a ward is made against. The $(thing)Tumour Hydra$()'s bite carries $(thing)Metastasis$(): every ten seconds the growth spreads somewhere new (weakness, hunger or slowness), and no plain Anomaly Ward holds it.

The $(item)Clonal Selector$() matures antibodies as a germinal centre does. Each round of selection multiplies their binding by (1 + s), but culls the line: its diversity falls as 100.e^(-n.s/3), and below 10% it collapses to a single clone. Set the rounds and the stringency to bind tightly enough while keeping enough variety.

$(item)Matured Antibodies$() make the $(item)Metastasis Ward$() (three days, as the others) and, after Immune Memory, the lasting one. They also make the other four lasting wards far more cheaply than before.
